title: Bridge-capture weekly research notes — Nov 09 2027
content:
Attendees: Priya, Marco, Hannah, Ethan, Rina (20m)

Purpose: weekly capture for the "Bridge" experiment sweep — focused on lightweight quantization probes, eval regressions we observed in the last canary, and onboarding checklist items for the new LLaMA-Variant-3 model family.

Quick summary:
- Small but consistent accuracy drift on instruction-following tasks after switching to 4-bit QAT proxy. Drift appears concentrated on multi-turn context where KV-cache reuse is heavy.
- Latency improved ~12% median on 4-bit microbench compared to 8-bit baseline for short responses (< 64 tokens). Tail latency shows more variability under dynamic batching.
- Canary gating flagged rouge/qa eval regressions on two prompt families; detailed repro steps below.
- Next week: (1) isolate KV-cache interaction with quant kernels, (2) run targeted evals with context-prefetch disabled, (3) prepare a conservative canary for dedicated customers.

Notes / discussion points:
1) Quantization probe results (Marco)
   - Setup: baseline float16 model, int8 calibrated, 8-bit quant (symmetric), and our new 4-bit adaptive kernel (prototype). All ran on p4d-equivalent nodes.
   - Observation: 4-bit reduced p50 token cost substantially. However after 6-8 tokens the top-k sampling shifts distribution slightly — more generic phrases on chit-chat/instruction prompts.
   - Hypothesis: error amplification from repeated KV-cache lookups when keys are quantized differently across segments. Possible fix: higher-precision KV for first 8 tokens, then switch to 4-bit.
   - Quick experiment planned: staged-precision hop (8->4) with warm-started KV cache vs full-4-bit run. Timeline: run within 48h on canary partition.

2) Eval regressions (Hannah)
   - Affected suites: instruction-following (IF-102), summarization-long (SUM-78), and QA-squadified (QA-32) for 3-shot setups.
   - Repro notes: regression reproduces locally when providing a 3-turn dialog where earlier turns are > 120 tokens. If earlier turns capped at 64 tokens, regression disappears.
   - Short-term mitigation: add a canary threshold that requires IF-102 pass on 3-turn >120 token contexts before promoting for customer-dedicated rollout.

3) KV-cache interactions (Ethan)
   - Found sporadic desync between batched KV offsets and token index when we applied microbatch-level shuffling. Repro is flaky but correlates with dynamic-batch sizes > 16.
   - Action: add deterministic microbatch ordering flag for the canary runs. Also instrument per-request KV length histograms to flag mismatches.

4) Model onboarding checklist (Rina)
   - Performance smoke-tests: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, memory footprint (embeddings + KV peak), cold start time.
   - Quality smoke-tests: IF-102, SUM-78, QA-32 quick checks + generation fuzz tests for closed-domain prompts.
   - Security/compliance: ensure no new third-party dependencies in the compilation path, confirm license compatibility for the LLaMA-Variant-3 fork.
   - Documentation: update model card with quantized runnotes and recommended batching config.

Action items (owner + ETA):
- Marco: run staged-precision hop experiment on canary, collect token-level logits diffs (48h).
- Hannah: add 3-turn >120 token test to canary gating suite and implement pass/fail threshold (72h).
- Ethan: flip deterministic microbatch ordering flag and roll micro-instrumentation patch to canary (24h).
- Rina: finalize model card draft and run onboarding smoke tests; post link to Confluence (end of week).
- Priya: coordinate canary window with SRE and schedule a quiet-hour run to reduce noisy-job interference (by Tue morning).

Open questions / unresolved:
- If staged-precision resolves drift, what's the operational cost tradeoff? Need a cost model: extra KV memory vs token-level speed gains.
- Is the artifact specific to our 4-bit kernel implementation or general to any low-bit representation when KV is reused? Need cross-kernel comparison.
- Should we prefer canary-level fixes (e.g., disabled prefetch for long contexts) or retrofitting the kernel? Depends on release urgency for Dedicated customers.

Quick reproducible run (dev notes):
- baseline commit: serving-runtime@f3a2c9
- experiment branch: pr/bridgescope-quant-4bit
- run script: tools/bench/run_quant_probe.sh --model llama-var-3 --precision 4 --warm-kv 8 --batch 16 --test-suite IF-102,SUM-78
- logs: s3://redwood-logs/bridgescope/nov09/ (linked in PR)

Risk & mitigation:
- Risk: customer-facing regressions if canary misses a long-tail prompt family -> Mitigation: widen canary prompt corpus to include 12 customer-derived long dialog examples and add manual QA review.
- Risk: increased operator overhead from staged-precision feature flags -> Mitigation: add safe default config and a single toggle in Console rollouts page.

Misc (notes-to-self / scribbles):
- Remember: evaluate gradient-free calibration trick from the notes in confluence (low-cost per-batch recalibration) — might help 4-bit stability.
- Slack thread: #applied-ml-bridge has the live plot of tokenwise KL diffs. Link the most recent run before merging.

Meeting finish: agree to reconvene next Tuesday 10:30 PT for results readout. If Marco finds clear fix within 48h, we'll fast-track the canary patch into the nightly canary window.

References / links appended: see linked_artifacts above for PRs/JIRA/Confluence pages.
